references.text: The basis for voluntary offerings to the sanctuary is established here, where the Lord commands Moses to receive gifts from everyone who has a willing heart.
Moses conveys the Lord's command that all with a willing heart should bring gifts to the sanctuary.
Summarizes that the Israelites brought voluntary offerings to the Lord, both men and women with willing hearts.
Describes how those who had wisdom in their hearts and a willing spirit came to do the work.
David rejoices that the people gave willingly with a whole heart for the building of the temple.
David acknowledges that the ability to give voluntarily comes from God, paralleling how the heart was lifted up in Exodus.
God stirred the spirits of the family heads so that they were willing to go up and build the house of the Lord, similar to how the Spirit moved the people to give.
The family heads gave voluntary gifts to the house of God, reflecting the voluntary giving in Exodus.
Paul teaches that when there is a willing heart, the gift is accepted according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
Each person should give as they have decided in their own heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
Complementary verses in the same chapter that together show the need for both wisdom and a willing heart in God's work.
